stem: You can use FMLA if you are adopting a child.
why: Placement of a child for adoption or foster care is an FMLA qualifying event (up to 12 weeks), completed within 12 months of the placement.

flashcard.front: Can you use FMLA if you are adopting a child?
flashcard.back: Yes. Adoption or foster care placement is a qualifying event.

keyFact: FMLA and adoption: yes, a qualifying event

stem: FMLA is optional if the employee qualifies.
why: FMLA is not discretionary. Once the employer knows leave is for an FMLA reason, it must designate it as FMLA leave, even without the employee's cooperation ("forced designation").

flashcard.front: Is FMLA optional if the employee qualifies?
flashcard.back: No. FMLA is not discretionary; the employer must designate qualifying leave.

keyFact: FMLA optional for a qualifying employee: No (not discretionary; forced designation)

stem: Harassment can be non-verbal.
why: Harassment may be physical, verbal, or non-verbal. Non-verbal examples include cartoons, posters, photographs, clothing, bumper stickers, and gestures.

flashcard.back: Yes. It may be physical, verbal, or non-verbal (cartoons, posters, gestures, etc.).

stem: Generally, FMLA requires an employer to provide eligible employees up to how many weeks of leave?
why: FMLA generally provides eligible employees up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a rolling twelve-month period.
keyFact: FMLA leave: up to 12 weeks, unpaid, job-protected, rolling 12-month period

stem: To be eligible for FMLA, an employee must have worked how many hours during the prior twelve months?
why: Eligibility depends on at least 12 months worked, 1,250 hours worked during the prior twelve months, and the reason for leave.
keyFact: FMLA hours requirement: 1,250 hours in the prior twelve months

stem: To be eligible for FMLA, an employee must have worked 12 consecutive months.
why: The employee needs at least 12 months worked, but not 12 consecutive months.
keyFact: FMLA months requirement: at least 12 months worked, not consecutive

stem: Under the FMLA definition of a "serious health condition," incapacity with continuing treatment by a health care provider must last more than how many days?
why: A serious health condition includes incapacity for more than three days with continuing treatment by a health care provider.
keyFact: Serious health condition incapacity: more than three days with continuing treatment

stem: An employee needs surgery to reset a broken limb. Under the "serious health condition" definitions, this might fit which category?
options: Restorative surgery after an accident or injury
Incapacity relating to pregnancy or prenatal care
why: Under conditions requiring multiple treatments, surgery to reset a broken limb or repair a torn ligament might fit restorative surgery after an accident or injury.

stem: Calling in "sick" without saying more is enough for the absence to qualify for Family and Medical Leave.
why: Calling in sick without saying more is insufficient for the absence to qualify for FMLA.

stem: If an employee gives unequivocal notice of intent not to return to work during FMLA leave, the employee is deemed to have voluntarily resigned at that time.
why: Unequivocal notice of intent not to return during FMLA leave means the employee is deemed to have voluntarily resigned at that time.

stem: How much notice of impending uniformed service should an employer generally expect from an employee?
options: 30 days or when orders are received, whichever is shorter
30 days or when orders are received, whichever is longer
14 days or when orders are received, whichever is shorter
60 days or when orders are received, whichever is longer
why: Generally expect thirty days notice or notice at the time the employee receives orders, whichever is shorter. Notice should include a copy of the orders.
keyFact: Uniformed services notice: 30 days or at receipt of orders, whichever is shorter

stem: Military (uniformed services) leave is paid leave.
why: Military leave is unpaid.

stem: Reemployment rights for returning service members are guaranteed up to a cumulative maximum of how many years of service?
why: Reemployment rights are guaranteed up to a cumulative maximum of five years of service, and in some instances that period can be extended.
keyFact: Reemployment rights: up to a cumulative 5 years of service

stem: A service member returns after years away on active duty. Reemployment must be prompt, which here means taking no more than:
why: After years of active duty the employer may take more time, but not more than two weeks. After one weekend of Guard training, the employee must be back the next working day.
keyFact: Prompt reemployment: next working day after a weekend; no more than 2 weeks after years of active duty

stem: Under the "escalator principle," a returning service member is returned to:
options: The position he or she would have held had he or she not been absent
The position he or she held at the time service began
Any open position at the same rate of pay
A position chosen by Human Resources
why: The service member is not returned to the position held when service began, but to the position he or she would have held without the absence, including bonuses, merit increases, shifts, and seniority.
keyFact: Escalator principle: returned to the position he or she would have held had there been no absence

stem: An eligible employee may take up to how many weeks of military caregiver leave to care for a service member with a serious injury?
why: Military caregiver leave is up to twenty-six weeks, and combined Family and Medical and Military Caregiver leave may not exceed 26 weeks in a rolling 12-month period.
keyFact: Military caregiver leave: up to 26 weeks (combined with FMLA, no more than 26 weeks in a rolling 12 months)

stem: To be a disability, an impairment only has to limit one major life activity.
why: The slide states that to be a disability, an impairment only has to limit 1 major life activity.
keyFact: Disability: impairment need only limit 1 major life activity

stem: Being regarded as having a "transitory" impairment does not qualify as a disability. A transitory impairment is one lasting:
why: Being regarded as having a transitory impairment, one lasting 6 months or less, does not qualify.
keyFact: Transitory impairment: lasting 6 months or less

stem: Which of these is NOT a reasonable accommodation?
options: Creating a new job for the employee
why: Creating a new job or allowing an employee to perform "odd jobs" around the department are not reasonable accommodations.

stem: The ultimate decision of whether a particular accommodation request is reasonable is left to the sound discretion of:
why: Per the slide, the ultimate decision on whether an accommodation request is reasonable is left to the sound discretion of the direct supervisor.

stem: A supervisor's romantic relationship with a subordinate may be considered harassment only if it is not consensual.
why: A supervisor engaging in a romantic relationship with a subordinate may be considered harassment whether consensual or not.

stem: Failure to promptly investigate and correct known or suspected harassment waives certain defenses for the employer.
why: All allegations should be investigated; failing to promptly investigate and correct known or suspected harassment waives certain defenses for your employer.

stem: Employees should not provide any employment references, positive or negative, regarding current or former employees.
why: One of the deck's nuggets: do not provide any employment references, positive or negative, regarding current or former employees.
